_doc: This is the machine-readable half of your project's contract with the loop.
The other half is the '## SDLC Contract' section of your CLAUDE.md: rules a
script cannot check, written for the assistant to read.
Nothing here starts the loop: a person does, by typing /sdlc:next in Claude Code.
Commands run from the repository root. Leave one empty to skip that step.
The coverage and mutation commands must print their percentage as the last
Run 'sdlc doctor' after changing anything here.
_commands_doc: Checked against Taskfile.yml, which is what CI runs as './task check'.
lint, fmt and fmt_check go through ./task so they use the golangci-lint the
Taskfile pins and the gofmt of the toolchain go.mod pins, not whatever is on PATH.
test is './task test' plus -count=1. npm_test is not one the loop runs by name:
it needs node on PATH, and is for a story that touches npm/.

commands.fmt_file: case "$FILE" in *.go) GOTOOLCHAIN="$(sed -n 's/^toolchain //p' go.mod | head -n 1)" go fmt "$FILE" >/dev/null ;; esac
commands.coverage: go test ./... -count=1 -coverprofile=.sdlc/state/cover.out >/dev/null && go tool cover -func=.sdlc/state/cover.out | tail -1 | grep -Eo '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'

_staffing_doc: Both lists are lowest first. The project manager chooses each agent's model
and effort from them, story by story; no 'lowest' is set, so nothing here
bring_back: the paths the contract names as high risk bring security back,
what runs on every tool call brings perf back, and what a person reads
brings the human advocate back, even where the staffing left them out.
